title: DHCP not handing out addresses
symptom: Many PCs on one floor have no network and show IP addresses starting with 169.254
user_description: Nobody on our floor has network since this morning. I checked my IP like you showed me once and it says 169.254 something. Is it all our cables?

options.text: Give every PC on the floor a fixed IP address by hand
options.why: This can cause address conflicts, bypasses how the network is managed, and leaves the real fault unfixed.

options.text: Replace the network cables on every PC
options.why: Many PCs failing at once points to something they share, not dozens of bad cables.

options.text: Reinstall the network drivers on each PC
options.why: The drivers work fine. A 169.254 address means the PC asked for an address and got no reply.

options.text: Recognise that 169.254 means the PCs got no address from DHCP; since the whole floor is affected, collect details and escalate to the network team to check the DHCP server or scope
options.why: When many PCs fail together, the cause is shared, such as the DHCP server, a full address scope or the floor switch. The network team can fix that in one place.

hints: What does an address starting with 169.254 tell you?
One PC or many: what does that point to?
Who looks after the DHCP server?
real_world_tip: A 169.254 address is called APIPA: Windows gives itself one when no DHCP server answers. Run ipconfig on two or three PCs to confirm before escalating.
